$comment: Hand-authored input for scripts/sync-skills.ts. Router descriptions are what skills-aware harnesses use to auto-invoke the category entry point — keep them trigger-rich and under 1024 characters. Workflow lines become the 'Typical workflow' section of the generated router SKILL.md.

help.shortDescription: List the CMSIS slash commands, VS Code commands, MCP tools and settings
help.description: List what the CMSIS Developer Assistant offers and which part fits a task: the CMSIS slash commands (cmsis-project, cmsis-bring-up, cmsis-pack, cmsis-debug-live, cmsis-pack-docs, add-board-layer) and the member skills behind each, the VS Code commands that register agents and select skills, the MCP tool groups for building, flashing and live Cortex-M debugging, and the settings that control the AI Skills Pack. Use when the user asks what CMSIS skills, commands or tools are available, which skill or tool to use for a CMSIS task, how to install more CMSIS skills, or how the CMSIS Developer Assistant is configured. Not a workflow itself — it points to the skill or tool that does the work.

commands.cmsis-developer-assistant.configure: The first-run setup, on demand: register the MCP server with the agents you pick, then choose the AI Skills Pack skills to install.
commands.cmsis-developer-assistant.selectSkills: Pick the AI Skills Pack skills (category entry points or individual skills) to copy into your personal skills directories.
commands.cmsis-developer-assistant.listTargetDocs: Write the current csolution target's documentation list (pack manuals, Arm documents, imported and workspace PDFs) to the output channel.
commands.cmsis-developer-assistant.indexTargetDoc: Extract and index every PDF of the current target now, with progress, so the first search is instant.
commands.cmsis-developer-assistant.importUserDoc: Copy PDFs the packs do not ship (NDA manuals, portal downloads) into the user documents folder, attributed to the current pack, device, board or core, and index them.
commands.cmsis-developer-assistant.openUserDocsFo: Reveal the user documents folder in the file manager.
commands.cmsis-developer-assistant.openPackDocsPa: Open the Pack Docs panel: the resolved target, its documents and their index state, the SVD peripherals, the page store, and a runner for the documentation tools.

toolGroups.name: CMSIS Solution actions
toolGroups.summary: `cmsis_action` — build, load, erase, load_and_run, load_and_debug, attach, detach, stop_run (the CMSIS Solution panel buttons); `flash` — program via pyOCD with a synchronous result.

toolGroups.name: Cortex-M
toolGroups.summary: `read_memory`, `read_core_registers`, `read_peripheral_register` (SVD), `lookup_peripheral` / `lookup_register` (SVD map and bit fields, no session needed), `get_fault_info` (CFSR/HFSR decode), `diagnose_fault` (one-call triage: frame, stack, address, hypotheses), `read_cycle_counter`, `get_device_info`.

toolGroups.name: Session health and windows
toolGroups.summary: `get_session_status`, `check_target_connection`, `get_debug_instructions`; with several VS Code windows `list_debug_windows` and `select_debug_window`.

toolGroups.name: Documentation (experimental, off by default — cmsis-developer-assistant.packDocs.enabled)
toolGroups.summary: `list_target_docs`, `search_target_docs`, `read_doc_pages`, `fetch_doc`, `get_peripheral_docs` — page-cited answers from the reference manuals, datasheets, errata and board manuals the target's packs ship or link, Arm documents, imported and workspace PDFs, and third-party part datasheets (sensors, ADCs) — start any part-number lookup here; fetch_doc indexes a PDF URL found on the web.

toolGroups.name: Build artefacts (experimental, off by default — cmsis-developer-assistant.buildInfo.enabled)
toolGroups.summary: `list_build_artifacts`, `get_memory_usage`, `lookup_symbol`, `get_section_layout`, `get_build_diagnostics` — the ELF, linker map and build log of the current target, read deterministically.

settings.installedSkills: The AI Skills Pack skills (entry points or individual skills) to copy into your personal skills directories; `cmsis-debug-live`, `add-board-layer` and `cmsis-help` are always installed.
settings.aiSkills.enabled: Install the AI Skills Pack at all. Off: pack skills this extension installed are removed, the skills setup step and the install prompt are skipped; the selection is kept.
settings.aiSkills.promptOnDetect: Offer to install the pack — at most once a month — when an agent has the MCP server registered but no pack skill is selected.
settings.packDocs.enabled: Experimental. Offer the documentation tools (list_target_docs, search_target_docs, read_doc_pages, fetch_doc, get_peripheral_docs) to agents. Off by default; needs pdftotext (poppler); window reload.
settings.buildInfo.enabled: Experimental. Offer the build-artefact tools (list_build_artifacts, get_memory_usage, lookup_symbol, get_section_layout, get_build_diagnostics) to agents. Off by default; window reload.

categories.label: CMSIS project setup
categories.shortDescription: Create, extend or retarget CMSIS csolution and Zephyr projects
categories.description: Set up and extend CMSIS csolution projects and Zephyr-based CMSIS solutions: verify the CMSIS-Toolbox, CMake, Ninja and compiler environment or a Zephyr west workspace; resolve a fuzzy board or device name to its exact CMSIS identity and BSP/DFP, or to its Zephyr board target; add a verified target to an existing *.csolution.yml; find compatible packaged board layers; or create an initial west-integrated CMSIS Zephyr Blinky solution. Use when the user wants to create, extend or retarget a csolution, check their build tools, or identify board, device and pack identifiers; this skill routes to the specialised project skills installed next to it. Not for debugging a running target (cmsis-debug-live) or for PDSC authoring (cmsis-pack).
workflow: `$check-cmsis-environment` (or `$check-zephyr-environment`) to confirm the toolchain before anything is created or built.
`$identify-cmsis-board-support` (or `$identify-zephyr-board`) to resolve the hardware to exactly one verified identity and its BSP/DFP.
`$add-cmsis-target` to extend the solution, then `$identify-cmsis-board-layer` for a packaged board layer — or `$start-zephyr-project` for a new west-integrated solution.

`$add-board-layer` when no packaged layer fits: interview for the few open decisions, then author Board.clayer.yml with its startup, stdio and memory files — or integrate the DFP's configuration generator — and build to green.

categories.label: Device debug and trace knowledge
categories.shortDescription: Establish verifiable device debug and trace facts from documentation
categories.description: Establish documentation-led, verifiable device debug and trace facts for an SoC or board before CMSIS-Pack debug content is authored: the debug access topology (processor association, debug-port and access-port path, protocol, dormant state), reset, unlock, authentication, boot, flash and low-power debug behaviour, CoreSight trace paths and components, board connector, jumper and pin-routing choices, supplementary pyOCD topology scans, pyOCD availability, and recovery of moved or broken vendor documentation URLs. Use when the user asks how a device is debugged, what its debug or trace topology is, wants a debug or trace knowledge record (.agent-artifacts) built or refreshed, or before generating PDSC debug or trace sequences; this skill routes to the specialised bring-up skills installed next to it. No live target connection is required; for a live session use cmsis-debug-live.
workflow: `$debug-access-knowledge` first — the access topology every other record builds on.
`$debug-knowledge` and/or `$trace-knowledge` for behaviour and trace facts; `$board-debug-knowledge` only for an explicitly board-specific question.
`$check-pyocd-availability`, then `$pyocd-detect-debug-topology`, when documentation leaves a required observation open.
`$resolve-official-device-documentation` whenever a vendor document link is dead or has moved.

categories.label: CMSIS-Pack debug authoring
categories.shortDescription: Author, validate and apply PDSC debug and trace sequences and debugvars
categories.description: Author and maintain CMSIS-Pack Debug Description content in a Device Family Pack PDSC: device-specific debug sequences (unlock, debug-port setup, reset, bootloader, flash, debug authentication, multi-core start, sleep and low-power), CoreSight trace sequences (TraceStart, TraceCapture, TraceFlush, TraceStop), <debugvars> runtime variables, and the non-sequence <debug>, <debugconfig>, debug-port and access-port definitions — each evidence-backed, validated, and applied only after the user confirms. Use when the user wants to add, change, review, validate or apply PDSC debug or trace sequences or debugvars for a device; this skill routes to the specialised pack-authoring skills installed next to it. Not for a live debug session (cmsis-debug-live) or for first establishing a device's debug facts (cmsis-bring-up).
workflow: Facts first: `$debug-access-knowledge`, then `$debug-knowledge` and/or `$trace-knowledge` (bring-up) must have produced their knowledge records.
`$prepare-pdsc-sequence-change` to scope the change, check inherited definitions and choose shared-versus-leaf placement.
`$apply-confirmed-pdsc-proposal` only after the user has explicitly confirmed the edits.
